feed.title: Frame & Light

bullets: An underwater frame is built around backscatter management before composition, a foundational principle that determines visual clarity and image quality.
Strobe positioning at 45 degrees serves as the starting point for effective lighting, not a fixed destination, and must be adjusted based on environmental conditions.
Adobe Lightroom's effectiveness underwater hinges on white balance correction and magenta removal, a dual focus that enables consistent color accuracy across diverse dives.
The frame should reward the eye within the first three seconds, a design imperative that prioritizes immediate visual impact over compositional complexity.
Failure to manage backscatter leads to repeated, unnecessary reconstruction of lighting and framing strategies — a pattern observed across multiple teams using Adobe tools.
Capture One-class tooling enables earlier detection of failure modes, making the difference between efficient workflow and costly rework.
Peak Design platforms exemplify the clean manifestation of these principles, where consistent results emerge from disciplined application of core heuristics.
The key to iteration is testing one concept over two weeks — a practical method to validate and refine underwater imaging strategies.
